claim: Syzygy can persist, create, join, reopen, and leave an explicitly disclosed bring-your-own WebSocket relay project while retaining local IndexedDB durability, but the bearer invitation does not authenticate people and Syzygy does not yet bundle or persist the relay.
commands: node scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm --prefix frontend run test:collaboration:websocket
node scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm --prefix frontend run test:network-boundaries
proved: The persisted manifest accepts only canonical WS/WSS endpoints and strong URL-safe bearer rooms; store v4 preserves the binding idempotently.
Product create/join controls require explicit acknowledgement that the invitation grants read/edit access and identities are self-reported.
A strict bounded invitation round-trips exact project/document/title/endpoint/room identity and rejects unsupported fields, oversize input, inactive projects, and malformed transports.
Offline project archives remove the endpoint and bearer room and reopen as independent local projects.

Two real WebsocketProjectProvider instances exchange updates through the pinned relay; one logical installation destroys and recreates its document/provider, restores from its own IndexedDB store, and synchronizes a new edit back.
Raw clients additionally converge partitioned edits after relay process replacement and remove disconnected awareness.
Dynamic WS/WSS CSP activation has matching source, copy, payload, and credential disclosure in the strict network-boundary manifest.
notProved: Authenticated participant identity, authorization roles, invitation revocation, or protection after an invitation leaks.
A bundled or one-click relay, durable server persistence, backup/restore, quotas, abuse controls, or hosted deployment operations.
Packaged CSP behavior, physical two-install use, five-client rapid-edit soak, hostile binary-frame fuzzing, cross-platform packet capture, or public WSS policy behavior.
A shipped updater artifact containing this implementation.
